title: Print a greeting
description: Use print() to show a greeting, such as Hello, Good morning, or Good afternoon. Any greeting is fine.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Anything you print is accepted. Use valid Python print(...) syntax.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with print any greeting. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Anything you print is accepted. Use valid Python print(...) syntax.

title: Comment a line of code
description: Write a comment on a line by starting it with #. For example: # This is my first comment. A comment does not need to print anything.
hints: Comments are ignored by Python, so no output is needed.
explanation: A comment starts with #. It is used to write a note in your code. Python does not run a comment, so it does not print anything.
commonMistakes: Do not forget # at the start of the comment. You do not need print() for this question.

validation.feedback: Start a line with # and write any comment.

title: Print your name and age
description: Use one print() statement to show your name and age together. You can choose any name and age.
hints: Read the task once and identify the Python feature it asks you to practise.
Try print("Name:", name), print("Name: " + name), or an f-string. These are all valid approaches.
Write your own code, press Run, and fix any syntax or runtime error shown.
explanation: This task gives you practice with print two values. The reference solution is only one example; other working approaches are accepted when they use the required Python feature.
commonMistakes: Check brackets and quotes, use the correct indentation, and make sure you actually use the Python feature asked for in the task.

validation.feedback: Display two pieces of information in one print() call. Multiple arguments, +, and f-strings are accepted.
